text:
anya: heads-up — I'm uploading a couple of nsys + perfetto traces from the KV-cache regression run. need consensus on naming, redaction rules, and where to put them. :eyes:
kevin: +1. where were you planning to store them? last time we used s3://redwood-internal/perf-traces but we had messy ACLs.
mike: s3 path is fine but please put them under /eng-runtime/profiling/ and mark sensitive as true if any customer ids leak. we should have a lifecycle policy (30d -> archive).
anya: planning: s3://redwood-internal/eng-runtime/profiling/2026-03-17/1760667890_ks-batch-kv-nsys.tar.gz and a perfetto .pb for timeline. also will include a small metadata.json with commit/model/seqlen/batch/kvcache_rate/kernel_hint.
lucas: naming nit: include model shortname and commit short SHA. e.g. 1760667890-gptj-8k-3e4f2a-ks-batch-kv-nsys.tar.gz. makes triage faster.
kevin: also add a human-readable "what to look for" file next to the trace: notes.txt with observed regression numbers (p95, p99, tokens/sec) and rough hypothesis.
anya: agreed. question on redaction: traces capture file paths, some mmap filenames include customer dataset paths. what's our standard scrub?
mike: run tools/scrub-trace.py --strip-paths --anonymize-ids on the raw perfetto proto and nsys export. that script replaces absolute paths, IPs, and token-like patterns. it also optionally drops args for execve.
anya: paste scrub command so others can reuse:
```
# from repo root
venv/bin/python tools/scrub-trace.py \
  --input trace_raw.pb \
  --output trace_scrub.pb \
  --strip-paths \
  --anonymize-ids \
  --drop-exec-args
```
kevin: good. add a small md5 of the scrubbed file in metadata so we can verify uploads.
lucas: for performance debugging we also want the kernel timeline csv (nsys export --csv) and the cupy/torch kernel names mapping. please include kernel_map.json produced by our trace-extract tool.
anya: note on metadata.json schema i used: {commit, model, model_variant, seq_len, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate, workload_desc, platform, gpu, driver, cudnn, kernel_profile_files: [list], scrubbed: true, notes_file}. will upload that too.
kevin: obligations: if trace contains customer PII even after scrub mark it as "restricted" and ping security for manual review. Do NOT post restricted traces in public channels.
lucas: how about perf-bot integration? can it automatically populate a short summary on upload?
perf-bot: I can. use perf-bot upload CLI: perf-bot upload --bucket eng-runtime --path 2026-03-17/1760667890 --meta metadata.json --public no. It will return a short viewer link and checksum.
anya: perfect. after upload I'll paste the viewer link into #eng-runtime and add the shortlist: commit+model+regression numbers. anyone doing analysis, annotate the trace in perfetto and leave notes in notes.txt so we keep context.
mike: analysis tips: when looking for kernel-selection regressions, filter perfetto for cudaDriverApi calls + kernel launches and compare kernel name prefixes vs previous-good trace. check KV cache hot/hit rates by searching for cache.get/cache.hit events we emit. batching issues often show up as lots of small kernels instead of merged big ones — look at launch timestamps clustering.
kevin: small suggestion: include a 1-2 line summary of "what to check first": 1) kernel name changes 2) unusual kernel durations 3) sudden drop in KV hit rate 4) batching count distribution. put it in notes.txt.
anya: uploading now (scrubbed). Using filename: 1760667890-gptj-8k-3e4f2a-ks-batch-kv-nsys.tar.gz and metadata uploaded next to it. perf-bot returned viewer: https://perfviewer.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/1760667890 (restricted: no).
lucas: thanks — i'll pull and do a quick diff vs good trace. will add annotations as I go. :thumbsup:
kevin: nice. one more ask: keep a changelog entry in /docs/trace-guidelines.md when we change scrub rules so audits are possible.
anya: will update docs after this upload. tagging @mike for follow-up on adding the scrub step to CI for long-running nightly traces.
mike: on it. thanks all.
